KZN Floods

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Devastating floods wreak havoc in KZN

Unique Selling Point:
We take a look at the devastating floods that have hit the KZN coastline this week. At the moment the official death toll is 51 - 9 people died in Chatsworth. Areas like Paddock, Amanzimtoti and Marburg on the South Coast were also hit hard.

Summary:
On Monday and Tuesday people of the KZN coast were battling a huge storm, some places measuring as much as 200mm of rain in a single day. Roads and houses have been washed away. We meet some of the locals affected.

Further information:
* Weather predictions: The current weather pattern is not unique - we have about 10 of them annually in Autumn or Spring (About 2 of those bring heavy rain and floods) Think Laingsburg, 1981.
It has pretty much gone it’s course and is moving out, should be gone by tomorrow. But has left great devastation.

* Besides widespread damamge to the South Coast, the storm also brought with it som eadditional problems for the South Coast…
WATER SERVICES UPDATE: PUMP STATIONS TEMPORARILY SHUT OFF DUE TO FLOODS
AREA SOUTH:
Due to the current heavy rains, the Umzimkhulwane River has came down with lot of debris and the river bank at the Bhobhoyi abstraction pump station has flooded. And as a result, we have temporarily shut off the pump station until floods subsides to mitigate pump damages that might take longer to repair.
Also with heavy rains in Drakensburg, Umzimkhulu River is expected to bring down more debris which will also affect the operations of the pump station.
Customers are urged to use water sparingly during this period while we await resumption of normal operations.
AREA NORTH:
The Umthwalume Water Treatment Works has also been shut off, due to high river inflows. — This means the sewage is going into the sea!!!
The plant will be back online once the rain subsides.

- So large areas of the South Coast are sitting without drinkable water. Or are affected by interrupted water supply.

Script:


KZN Floods






VO
Images that that have gone viral on social media this week... (UPSOUND TOTI GOLF COURSE)

Torrential rains battered our country's Eastern coastline causing widespread flooding, mudslides … and the loss of many lives.
LINK
This is what Durban beaches look like after the storm. The affected areas start from Durban North and stretch all the way down to the Eastern Cape to Port St Johns.
VO
Just south of the city, in Amanzimtoti, residents are still in shock as houses simply collapsed when the ground gave way...
Angel Beetham
This is insane, you don't expect something like this to happen.
VO
Angel Beetham's family owns the house on the left. The property is rented out and fortunately the tenants managed to escape unharmed, but the house, as well as the one next door, lie in ruin...
Angel Beetham
I was in Cape Town and when Blue security phoned me I got the shock of my life – to say that it was our house that had gone down.
V/O
Durban should expect around 70mm of rain in an average month of April…but on Monday, more than a 100mm were recorded in some places... in just 24 hours.
VO
By early Tuesday morning a waterfall of mud and debris came crashing down the banks of a Chatsworth hillside. The road was washed away as the debris powered its way through the houses.
Siven
We heard this loud noise in the morning, the water just started to gush down into the house, but we managed to leave at that time.
Les Govender
In the early hours of the morning, when that entire bank washed down there and the water pipes underneath burst and took this entire section of the road out, into these houses down here. If we just look down here you'll see the damage that has been done onto this house. Onto this house and into the houses below that.
VO
Local member of parliament, Les Govender sees himself as a “community servant”.
Les Govender
All of these houses at the bottom have been swamped with mud and and the water that came down via that wash-away.
V/O
Besides losing their homes and many belongings, essential basic services have also been disrupted because of the flooding.
Les Govender
As a result now you will find this entire section of houses on the top here, they do not have fresh water supply. All these pipes have been damaged.
VO
A little further up the road tragedy struck as an embankment at a school came crashing down on the caretaker's home.
Les Govender
When that bank collapsed it came down and flattened this house and the people that were living in there didn't stand a chance.
LINK
Seven people lost their lives on this site where a brick structure once stood … but all that's left is mangled furniture, mud and rubble.
V/O
The Department of Cooperative Governance said 85 people died as a result of floods since Easter, including worshippers trapped in a church when the roof collapsed.

Although the amount of rainfall was unprecedented, Prof Francois Engelbrecht from the Wits Global Change Institute says the storm itself was nothing out of the ordinary.
Francois Engelbrecht
About 10 of these systems move into South Africa every year and about 1 out of 5 of these cut-off low pressure systems bring flooding to South Africa.
V/O
But with climate change, Engelbrecht says weather patterns are becoming more unpredictable.
Francois Engelbrecht
One thing that we can observe world-wide is that storm systems are generally becoming more intense and when they do occur they tend to cause more rainfall in the past.
VO
To mitigate high-rainfall storms in cities, the water has to go somewhere…

Several residents put blame for the extensive flooding on failing stormwater infrastructure.
Les Govender
CLAIRE: Could this have been prevented?

It most certainly could have been. If the municipality had been maintaining the drainage system in this area, if the stormwater drains have been cleared of debris in the past then they would have been able to accommodate the volume of water. But unfortunately that has not been happening and that is when you find that wen these floods came the storm water drainage couldn't handle the capacity ..
Willemien van Niekerk
Better infrastructure that are well-maintained, that have the capacity to carry the stormwater will certainly make a difference in terms of the exposure to people to these kinds of extreme rainfall events, but I do not think it's as simple as that.
VO
At the CSIR’s urban and regional planning group, senior researcher Willemien van Niekerk believes the solution lies in communities and municipalities working together better, to maintain infrastructure...

Litter, she says, has a severe impact on the effectiveness of stormwater drainage infrastructure.
Willemien van Niekerk
It threatens the natural ecosystem, it blocks the stormwater drainage and all of that has an impact on the whole drainage system of the municipality.
VO
Van Niekerk says the vast amount of waste washed up on beaches points to sub-optimal drainage.
VO
By Thursday the storm had dissipated and clean-up operations were well underway.

Carte Blanche offered the eThekwini Municipality an opportunity to respond to these allegations, but was referred to the Department of Cooperative Governance, who in turn said they were consumed with rescue efforts at this point.
Les Govender
CLAIRE: What's been done to help the people that were affected in this area?

We have established a relief centre at a church not far away from here and at the church we are housing some people that needed a shelter to stay for the past few days and we're also using that as a collection point for relief aid that have been coming in very generously from sponsors all over the place...
Rev Naidoo
We're reaching out to well over 800 to 1000 people by way of meals and various items that are of necessity.
VO
Together with a group of residents, Rev Jonathan Naidoo has been working around the clock to reach people who have been left displaced.

I am so grateful to god that we have a team of passionate volunteers. They are doing this to serve humanity with no strings attached.
VO
Because local government is key in helping residents adapt for future storms, beyond the clean-up, the CSIR has just launched a climate risk profiling and adaptation tool, called the Green Book.

If Durban had this information at hand, they could have put systems in place to support the drainage infrastructure... potentially resulting in much less damage and loss of lives.
Willemien van Niekerk
For every municipality in SA we have developed a risk profile, so municipalities can see their vulnerability, in terms of social, economic and environmental.
VO
The state-of-the-art “open access” online application is being introduced to municipalities and offers a range of tools to help local government with its long-term planning...
Willemien van Niekerk
Based on your specific risk profile you can elect through a filter those adaptation actions that municipalities can integrate within their urban planning and settlement design strategies and plans for the future to adapt urban areas to climate change.
VO
With the damage from Cyclone Idai far from cleaned up, and Kenneth wreaking havoc in Northern Mozambique right now…and the devastation across KZN…the CSIR urges municipalities and communities to take steps to make human settlements more resilient to severe weather.







PROMO 1 11”
This week parts of KZN were devastated by unprecedented rainfall. Houses were destroyed and and lives were lost. How do we mitigate the effects of the next storm?


PROMO 2 11”
At least 85 lives were lost this week in KwaZulu-Natal as severe storms brought rivers of mud and debris crashing through people's houses...


PROMO 3 11”
Earlier this week, the KZN coastline was battered by unprecedented rainfall, reminding us that adapting our cities to climate change is becoming a priority to help prevent similar future disasters.
